sections.heading: Welcome to the St. Philomena’s Placement Cell

content.text: At St. Philomena’s College, our Placement Cell is dedicated to empowering students to achieve their career aspirations and connect with top employers. We are committed to providing comprehensive support across all our programs, including UG, PG, MBA, and MCA placements.

1. Placement and Recruitment:○ We serve as the vital link between students and the professional world. Our Placement and Recruitment wing facilitates interactions between potential employers and our talented students, creating a dynamic environment for successful career placements.2. Training and Internship:○ Our Training and Internship wing is designed to equip students with the necessary skills and experience to thrive in their chosen careers. We offer tailored training sessions, workshops, and internship opportunities that foster personal and professional growth.3. Career Guidance:○ With a focus on individual aspirations, our Career Guidance wing provides personalized support to help students identify their passions and chart a path toward their career goals. We offer one-on-one counseling and resources to guide students in making informed decisions about their future. Whether you are a student seeking guidance or an employer looking to connect with bright minds, the Placement Cell at St. Philomena’s is here to assist you.
Reach out to us with any queries or for more information:Mr. MadanShaivaPRO & PO+91 6364118983[email protected]

Anti Ragging

content.text: St. Philomena’s Degree College (Autonomous) Mysore is committed in fostering a safe and inclusive learning environment for all its students. In pursuit of this commitment, the college has established an Anti-Ragging Committee to ensure the well-being of students and to create a campus culture that promotes respect, tolerance, and camaraderie.

items: Prevention of Ragging:To create awareness and prevent incidents of ragging within the campus.
Education and Sensitization: To educate students about the consequences of ragging and sensitize them to the impact it can have on victims.
Prompt Action: To promptly address any reported cases of ragging and take appropriate action against the perpetrators.
Orientation Programs: Conducting orientation programs at the beginning of each academic year to educate students about the college’s policies on ragging.
Awareness Campaigns: Organizing awareness campaigns throughout the year to emphasize the importance of maintaining a ragging-free environment.
Grievance Redressal: Providing a platform for students to report incidents of ragging and ensuring that prompt and appropriate action is taken.
Counselling and Support: Offering support and counselling services to victims of ragging and taking steps to rehabilitate them.
Regular Monitoring: Regularly monitoring different areas of the campus, especially during the initial days of the academic year, to prevent any potential incidents of ragging.

Action Against Offenders: The Anti-Ragging Committee is empowered to take strict disciplinary action against any individual or group found guilty of ragging, in accordance with the college’s policies and the laws of the land.

sections.heading: “You’re Not Alone — We’re Here for You.”

content.text: At St. Philomena’s College, Bannimantap, we understand that student life can be overwhelming. Whether you’re facing academic stress, personal struggles, or just need someone to talk to — our Counseling Center is a safe, confidential space where you’ll be heard and supported.

College is a time of growth, but it can also bring anxiety, uncertainty, and emotional challenges. The Counseling Center at Philomena’s is here to walk with you — through the highs and lows. Let’s talk. Let’s heal. Together.

Life doesn’t come with a manual, but we’re here to guide you. Our trained counselors help students build resilience, manage emotions, and rediscover their strength. Drop by the Counseling Center anytime — we care aboutyou.

Struggling in silence? You don’t have to. Our doors are open to every student who needs someone to talk to — without judgment, without pressure. Let the Counseling Center be your space for peace, clarity, and hope.

No issue is too small. Whether it’s exam pressure, relationship concerns, anxiety, or identity questions — we’re here to support your well-being. Your story matters. Your future matters. And you matter — always.

It is a voluntary humanitarian organization that encourages students aged 18 to 25 to engage in activities that promote health, service, and friendship. The YRC aims to instill a sense of social responsibility and humanitarian values among the youth, preparing them to respond to emergencies and contribute positively to society.

Facilities

sections.heading: Maintenance and Utilization of Physical, Academic, and Support Facilities

content.text: At our institution, we uphold a strong commitment to the optimal utilization and systematic maintenance of all physical, academic, and support facilities, including laboratories, libraries, sports complexes, computer systems, and classrooms. This approach ensures a well-maintained, safe, and conducive environment for academic excellence and holistic development.

General maintenance of the college infrastructure—including buildings, classrooms, and laboratories—is carried out by a dedicated team of skilled personnel, including plumbers, electricians, and carpenters, all working under the guidance of a facility supervisor. Garden upkeep is managed by an experienced team of gardeners who help maintain the aesthetic and ecological value of the campus.

Housekeeping services are outsourced to a professional agency. A housekeeping manager oversees the operations of a team responsible for daily sweeping, swabbing, and maintaining cleanliness across all academic and administrative blocks, twice a day.

The daily functioning and upkeep of the campus infrastructure are diligently supervised by the Rector, Vice Rector, and Campus Administrator. Their combined efforts ensure that the campus remains safe, clean, and fully functional at all times.

All laboratory equipment is insured and regularly serviced under Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs) with trusted external service providers. These contracts are closely monitored and renewed periodically to ensure uninterrupted academic operations.

Critical utilities such as elevators, air conditioners, CCTV surveillance systems, water purifiers, power generators, and UPS units are covered under AMCs and undergo regular inspection and maintenance. Waste management—including collection, segregation, and disposal—is efficiently handled by an internal team to promote sustainability and environmental responsibility.

Our IT infrastructure is managed by a team of qualified system administrators who are responsible for maintaining computer laboratories, the campus-wide network, and the official college website. Computers and related hardware are covered under AMCs with vendors to ensure timely servicing. All software used across the campus is properly licensed and routinely updated to stay current with technological advancements.

The maintenance of our sports infrastructure is overseen by a team comprising the Physical Education Director, the Sports Secretary, and support staff. This includes regular care of the indoor stadium, outdoor fields, and multi-gym. Daily tasks such as watering and rolling of the grounds, de-weeding, and track preparation ensure that the sports facilities are always in top condition. A certified gym instructor manages and maintains the multi-gym facility for safe and effective use by students.

Our college library is maintained in a clean and dust-free environment by the housekeeping team and support staff. Their responsibilities include regular mopping, sweeping, and dusting of furniture and books. A Library Committee, led by the Librarian, oversees the library’s day-to-day operations and infrastructure upkeep. Responsibilities such as maintaining the stock register, organizing books and journals, and updating the issue register are diligently carried out to ensure an efficient and student-friendly learning space

sections.heading: St Philomena’s Rovers and Rangers Unit

items: Home
St Philomena’s Rovers and Rangers Unit

content.text: The Bharat Scout & Guide is a voluntary, non-political, and educational movement that aims to develop young people in various aspects of their lives. This report focuses on the activities carried out by the Rover and Ranger unit of St. Philomena’s College, led by Mr. Mathew C as the Rover Leader and Dr. Sowmya as the Rangers Leader.

The purpose of the Bharat Scout & Guide movement is to contribute to the holistic development of young individuals, enabling them to reach their full potential physically, intellectually, emotionally, socially, and spiritually. The movement follows the purpose, principles, and methods established by Lord Baden Powell in 1907. It emphasizes inclusivity, welcoming young people from all backgrounds, irrespective of their origin, race, or creed.

The Rover and Ranger unit of St. Philomena’s College comprises a total of 30 students, with 18 rovers and 12 rangers. The unit provides a platform for these young individuals to engage in meaningful activities, develop essential life skills, and contribute to their communities.

In the academic year 2021-22, the Rangers and Rovers from St. Philomena’s College had the opportunity to participate in the International Cultural Jamboree held at Moodbidre. This event provided a unique cultural exchange platform for young people from different countries, promoting understanding, friendship, and global citizenship.

The unit actively engages in organizing health camps, recognizing the significance of physical well-being. These health camps aim to raise awareness about various health issues, promote preventive measures, and provide basic healthcare services to the underprivileged. Through these initiatives, the students learn about healthcare systems and develop empathy and compassion for those in need.

St. Philomena’s College unit of the Bharat Scout & Guide also actively participates in blood donation camps. By encouraging students to donate blood, the unit helps address the constant demand for blood in hospitals and supports life-saving treatments. This activity not only instills a sense of responsibility and altruism but also raises awareness about the importance of blood donation within the college community.

sections.heading: Cleanup Drive on World Environment Day:

content.text: To commemorate World Environment Day, the Rover and Ranger unit organizes a cleanup drive. This initiative aims to create awareness about environmental issues, such as pollution and waste management. By actively participating in the cleanup drive, students contribute to the local community’s cleanliness, fostering a sense of responsibility towards the environment.

The unit arranges special invited talks for students to inculcate values and develop essential skills. These talks provide a platform for experts and experienced individuals to share their knowledge, experiences, and insights. By exposing the students to diverse perspectives, the talks help broaden their horizons, enhance their understanding of various subjects, and inspire them to become responsible citizens.

The Bharat Scout & Guide unit at St. Philomena’s College, led by Mr. Mathew C, the Rover Leader and Dr. Sowmya, the Ranger Leader, have been actively engaged in promoting the holistic development of young individuals. Through their participation in international events, health camps, blood donation drives, cleanup activities, and special invited talks, the students have gained valuable experiences, skills, and values. These initiatives contribute to their growth as responsible citizens.

ncc.title: NCC – St. Philomenas College (Autonomous)

items: Home
NCC

sections.heading: Bird's Eye view of NCC in St Philomena’s College, Mysuru

content.text: NCC (National cadet corps) is the best organization to teach discipline, self-confidence, service motto, leadership qualities etc. There are infantry, artillery and naval wing. Our college had all the three branches from time to time. During the Principal Rev. Fr. N.T Thomas in 1962 an artillery unit was started, Mr. K.J Francis of Botany department and Mr. P.T Joseph of political science department were Commissioned as officers.

Hundreds of students were trained in those days, some of the cadets were honored as best cadets and promoted as under officers, some of the cadets passed B and C certificate examinations. Many cadets were sent to different courses, camps and the college unit achieved name and fame by all these activities.

Regular parades were held in the college, cadets were thought to use of rifle also shooting competitions were held locally.  There was a firing range at the back of our college near sports grounds where hundreds of cadets were trained in shooting the Bulls Eye.

Navel unit was started in 1966 by Lieutenant General Nagabhushanachari of Chemistry department. The cadets represented the college even in Republic Day parade in Delhi. They were thought ship modeling, boat pulling and sailing etc.

Infantry was a very popular unit in our college. Major Ranganath Rao the physical director and Major Ashwath Narayan professor of mathematics were in charge of infantry. They were even deputed as full time Army officers for 3 years during the war with neighboring countries. Major Ashwath Narayan was even honored with many awards by the government.

Professor K Shrinivasa Rao of Zoology department was in charge of ladies wing. He was succeeded by Professor M.C Prabha of the department of History, who was the first Lady lecturer of the college and served for 50 years continuously (1967 to 2017). As she was in NCC and passed the examination as a Cadet with Under Officer rank, she was Commissioned directly as commanding officer with the rank 2/Lieutenant. During her refresher course in Gwalior she fired from AK-47 rifle. She carried on the ladies wing for 3 years and she was sent to Himalayan Mountaineering training at Darjeeling and she was guided by none other than Tenzing Norgay the first man to climb the Mount Everest. She climbed Vidhanachandra peak at the height of 18,000ft, she was the captain during the training. Advanced mountaineering course was attended by under Officer Nirmala Patrick and other lady cadets represented the college during the Republic Day parade.

Infantry of ladies wing was discontinued after Lt M.C Prabha left NCC, but boy’s wing of our college continued its service under the leadership of different NCC officer like Lt Vidyadhar Sanjay Nair of department of Mathematics and Mr. Thomas Gunaseelan of Physics department. The cadets have attended even National Integration camps; many prices like best Marching award have been taken by cadets during the previous years.

NCC units of SPC have made tremendous progress as the training is very comprehensive and interesting because of Map Reading, unit defence, field engineering, weapon drill and parade. Now currently we have 3 KAR NAVAL UNIT NCC and 1 KAR ARTILLERY BATTERY NCC being very active under the present officers Mr. Eliezer Vishwas of Physics department and Mr. Francis Devasahayam B of Criminology and Forensic Science department respectively. Let the NCC units fly high and high in the coming years under the new officers.
Report by,
Mr. Eliezer Vishwas,Assistant Professor,Department of Physics,NCC officer – 3 KAR NAVAL UNIT NCC,St. Philomena’s College (Autonomous), Mysore.
